title: What are people thinking uploading literal slop to nextfest?
author: CourseSpare7641
selftext:
I mean seriously, do some game designers just not have any objective perception of quality? Are they not able to critically look at the game they made and judge if it's good or slop?

  
Yeah yeah nextfest is flooded. Whatever. If you put in even a modicrum of effort into actually crafting your game none of that junk is your competition. Their bar is so low that you'll step right over it and stand out.

I'm pretty optimistic all things considered.

comments.author: glimsky
comments.body: You make 10 games at $20 in AI costs plus the $100 Steam fee. If they each make $250 in lifetime revenue, you just made more than a grand for very little effort. I'm not saying the will make this much, but it's not an unreasonable thing to try.

replies.author: Shalke97
replies.body: You are forgetting The 30% Cut and taxes. Its Not that easy, believe me

replies.author: glimsky
replies.body: Fair enough regarding the numbers. But the principle stands: there must be a nontrivial number of people trying to make quick bucks by scaling out the number of games they make. Forget $250 per game from my example. If one game happens to make 2-3K because it becomes a surprising hit, they still make some easy money with very little effort. I'm not saying they will succeed, but trying makes sense.

comments.author: geddy
comments.body:
As it turns out, people who don’t know how to make games still suck at making games, even though they have tools to do it for them now!

From what I’ve learned here, people really don’t know how to make games. Very, very few exceptions. I’m not claiming to be an expert on the subject either, but holy crap are people making garbage. This is why our memory is expensive!?

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body:
It reminds me of when home video cameras became available.

Suddenly the tools to make a movie were widely accessible.

Not the same thing as the talent and skill to make a movie, though.

At the end of the day, talent + dedication is always needed to win. The tools getting easier doesn't change that - the tools got easier \*for everyone\* - it's not a leveling of the playing field, it's the same playing field - whoever puts in the most effort and has the most talent is still going to be on top.

And entertainment is necessarily zero-sum - you cannot be playing 2 people's games at once, so the market for games is fixed - this doesn't make it easier to win in gaming at all, it just raises the pace.

replies.author: FlightFit335
replies.body: And yet there's Tiktok today with all its human slop and views.

replies.author: FlightFit335
replies.body: No. Our memory is expensive due to manufacturing shortage.  Take time to separate the two.

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body:
Remember nfts? Crypto? 

Grifters come out the woodworks with every new technology in hope to make a quick buck. And some will. Some will make BIG quick bucks. But that'll very quickly fade as markets become familiar with said new technology.

Eventually, the grifters will get bored and tired because nobody is buying their slop and they'll move onto another industry they can ruin im hopes of a quick buck.

I know the nextfest number are wild this year. But I actually think they'll go down next year (still up in the long term, with a bit of a decline in the short term as this trend falls off).

We're in a new era. The real power isn't in the hands of games being generated In a Day, it's in the hands of indie teams of 5 - 20 people who dedicate 2 - 5 years to make a masterpiece they never could have before.

That era is a year or two out because the real chefs are still in the kitchen, watching the marketplace catch fire and waiting for their time to bring out a brand new cuisine.

comments.body:
They're having fun. Just look at the top lists, recommendations and reviews to find the good stuff as you always have.

During the next sale you're going to see thousands of new titles for under a dollar. Like a penny arcade. There'll be some gems in there, you might even be surprised that a game that looks like crap can actually have some good ideas that are fun. Imagine seeing Minecraft or rimworld for the first time today and dismissing it as slop.
